original.title: An Ice-Covered Ocean on Snowball Earth — Where Might Life Hide? 🧊
original.banner: Earth freezes over. Where does life hide?
original.hook_vo: An ocean sealed by ice. Where could life survive?
original.art_direction: Glacial cyan and white under a pale dim sun, crystalline ice textures, macro-to-wide contrast, black abyss below.

options.label: Inside a frozen wave
options.image_prompt: A towering breaking wave frozen solid on a white Cryogenian sea, crystal-blue ice curling overhead, pale dim sun behind, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from the low sun

options.label: Frozen shoreline boulders
options.image_prompt: Ice-glazed boulders on a frozen shoreline of bare rock, no plants anywhere, white sea ice to the horizon, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from a pale sunset

options.label: Snowfield at the equator
options.vo: On the equator's frozen snow field.
options.image_prompt: A blinding white snowfield stretching flat to every horizon on the Cryogenian equator, a small cold sun overhead, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from the small sun

options.label: Deep hydrothermal vent
options.vo: Sink to a deep hydrothermal vent.
options.image_prompt: A deep-ocean hydrothermal vent chimney in dark liquid water, dark mineral-rich fluid rising into cold seawater, pale microbial mats visible on the surrounding rock, no boiling bubbles, no molten rock, no glowing chimney, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from soft amber cinematic fill on the nearby pale minerals

options.label: Drifting ice floe
options.vo: A slab of drifting sea ice.
options.image_prompt: A cracked ice floe drifting on a slushy grey-white sea under a pale sky, sharp blue fractures, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from a weak low sun

options.label: Glacier crevasse
options.image_prompt: natural-history documentary view looking down into a deep blue glacier crevasse, walls of layered ice vanishing into darkness, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from faint sunlight from above

options.label: Frozen salt flat
options.image_prompt: A frozen salt flat cracked into hexagons of ice and white crust, wind-blown snow streaming, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from a pale orange sun

options.label: Top of the ice sheet
options.vo: Climb to the top of the ice sheet.
options.image_prompt: The crest of a kilometre-thick ice sheet under a black star-filled sky, wind tearing snow off the edge, photoreal painterly, vertical composition, one warm focal light from a thin dawn glow

original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 4, because scientists propose life used chemicals near deep sea vents to survive. A possible refuge beneath the ice.

fact.text: One proposed refuge for life during Snowball Earth was deep-ocean hydrothermal vents powered by chemicals rather than sunlight.
fact.source_sentence: In reservoirs of anaerobic and low-oxygen life powered by chemicals in deep oceanic hydrothermal vents surviving in Earth's deep oceans and crust; but photosynthesis would not have been possible there.

original.description: Hundreds of millions of years ago, ice may have reached the equator. Eight places for life to wait out Snowball Earth, and the one scientists keep coming back to.
original.related_topic_hint: Snowball Earth: The Planet That Froze
